gaps.sentence: As soon as the plane landed, everyone ___ their phones.
gaps.hint: as soon as links two past actions
gaps.explanation: 'As soon as' links two sequential completed actions, so the past simple is used: switched on.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: Wait there and I ___ you some aspirin.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous offer at the moment
gaps.explanation: Offers made spontaneously at the moment of speaking use 'will': will get.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: The bus ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
gaps.hint: official timetables use the present simple
gaps.explanation: Official timetables take the present simple for future events: leaves.
